thread.title: Opportunity Or Threat? It All Lies In The Eyes Of The Beholder And The Portfolio Of The Holder

author: The Fortune Teller
title: Opportunity Or Threat? It All Lies In The Eyes Of The Beholder And The Portfolio Of The Holder
text:
A lively discussion about immigration has developed along the thread of a recent article , where I touched upon banks on both sides of Atlantic with an emphasis on the leading (and troubled) Deutsche Bank ( DB ).
Immigration, trade wars, tariffs and geographical diversification are all part of globalization (and, let's face it, violence and shift of power); people move (relocation), money moves (transfer of wealth), operations move (geographical expansion) and even leaders move... Well, some more than others...
In any case, the discussion about immigration has led me to think on various aspects of "moving"/changing. Unsurprisingly, not every change end up positively and in some cases, a certain change, for itself, involves ever-changing outcomes.
Moreover, a change is not being perceived equally by all those who witness/experience it. While one may see a change as a potential threat another see the exact same change as an opportunity...
It may seem a but brutal/cruel but that's the world we live in. For good and for bad.
Similarly, when it comes to stocks - some of the changes/myths don't always work out as one would hoped/expected...
Diversification? Don't make me laugh... Who need diversification (when you pick the right names)?...
HEAR Total Return Price data by YCharts
YTD market-cap greater than $100M top performers:
Turtle Beach ( HEAR ) NII Holdings ( NIHD ) Tandem Diabetes Care ( TNDM ) Intelsat ( I ) Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals ( ARWR ) BlueLinx Holdings ( BXC ) Endocyte ( ECYT ) Fossil Group ( FOSL ) Arqule ( ARQL ) Madrigal Pharmaceuticals ( MDGL ) eGain ( EGAN ) Genesis Healthcare ( GEN ) Same sector, yet very different outcomes We already wrote about specific European banks - DB and the leading Spanish banks Banco Santander ( SAN ) and BBVA ( BBVA ) - that we avoid. But how about the banking system in the US (as a whole) vs Europe?
Well, when you put the Financial Select Sector SPDR® ETF ( XLF ) against iShares MSCI Europe Financials ETF ( EUFN ) over the past 7 years (exactly; since the 235th independence day) you see something quite rate when it comes to one sector with two very different outcomes.
EUFN data by YCharts
Growth - it's all about location The slowdown in the Eurozone is already clear. Many blame seasonal one-offs, the weather, etc.; anything except for the real reason: massive government, i.e. central bank, intervention and lack of real-effective reforms.
Meanwhile, across the ocean, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow - a running estimate of real GDP growth based on available data for the current measured quarter - is forecasting an over 4% growth in the US for Q2/2018.
Location, location, location... When it comes to real estate it's all about location. What about stocks? It seems like the answer is quite similar...
...or (almost) no location at all? This is a fantastic chart, showing you how online e-commerce - Amazon ( AMZN ), Alibaba ( BABA ), JD.com ( JD ), eBay ( EBAY ),, Rakuten ( OTCPK:RKUNY , OTCPK:RKUNF ), Zalando ( ZNDO , OTCPK:ZLNDY ), Groupon ( GRPN ) and the like - has grown compare to brick and mortar retailers such as Macy's ( M ), Sears Holdings ( SHLD ), Dillard's ( DDS ), J.C. Penney ( JCP +3.1%), Tailored Brands ( TLRD ), Tilly's ( TLYS ), Urban Outfitters ( URBN ), Guess ( GES ), Chico's FAS ( CHS ), DSW ( DSW ) and Express ( EXPR )
Speaking of which,
Separating the wheat from the chaff It's all about buybacks, especially when it comes to technology ( QQQ , XLK , VGT ), financials (XLF, VFH , KRE ), healthcare ( XLV , IBB , VHT ) and consumer discretionary ( XLY , VCR )
Where would this market be without corporations buying their own stocks?
Same sector - different sizes My new article about the FAANG stocks has drawn a bit of anger among those investing in Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and Alphabet's Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
Even if we don't pick on the technology sector ( QQQ , XLK ) as a whole, it's hard to ignore/dispute that within the sector, there's a significant divergence between large caps and small caps relative to their 52-week highs.
Source: Bespoke Investment Group
Is it absolute or relative value/strength we're looking at/searching for?...
Trade war Minimal impact? It depends...
Epilogue On any of the following topics, ask yourself: Good of bad? Absolute or relative?
Immigration (and what if we call it cheap labor force?...) High return (and what if we call it ultra high risk?...) Globalization (and what if we call it lack of national identity?...) Diversification (and what if we call it protection against ignorance?...) Trade war (and what if we call it a noble fight for justice?...) At the end of the day, it all lies in the eyes of the beholder... and the portfolio of the holder...
